correctness.rationale: In the sign-pair coordinates the heading generator is the sum of two rate-γ flip generators, even though a fixed sense of turn does not always flip the same bit. Orthogonal Brownian rotation and stationary OU filtering therefore give two independent copies, each X=Z+δG with Gaussian variance δ²=μD/v₀². In the athermal scalar stationary equations the total current vanishes, giving P_+−P_−=z(P_++P_−); substitution into either component equation gives the stated beta density and E[S|Z]=Z. The posterior sign for x>0 follows by pairing z with −z: the integrand contains g(x−z)−g(x+z)>0; by symmetry the opposite sign holds for x<0. With simultaneous thermal and sensor noise, the convolved kernel is still strictly decreasing in |x|: express the symmetric decreasing sensor density as a positive mixture of centered interval indicators; each Gaussian-smoothed nondegenerate interval is strictly decreasing for x>0. At zero noise the posterior mean equals the observed coordinate on its support. The factorized MAP signs give the four sectors and null decision boundaries. Conditioning the sign-success indicator on Z gives the erf integral; the product rule gives p². Differentiating the Gaussian convolution gives the score formula and the posterior mean derivative Var(Z|X=x)/δ². The beta integral gives the displayed γ-function ratio at zero noise, monotone likelihood-ratio order for Z² gives strict β monotonicity, and the erf integrand gives strict δ monotonicity. Independently integrating the uniform-coordinate case β=1 gives p=0.727536119397839 at δ=.3, hence p²=0.5293088050284667; at δ=0 the exact result is 9/16. Replay of the .3 case: python3 /workspace/branches/independent-boundary-checks.py. For fixed positive δ, Taylor expansion uses E Z²=(2β+1)^−1 and E Z⁴=O(β^−2). In the joint limit, √(2β)Z tends to N(0,1) with uniformly bounded second moments, so joint convergence with the scaled noise and uniform integrability justify the linear-growth expectation, including λ=0. For independent standard normals G,H, conditioning G on G+λH gives E[G sign(G+λH)]=√(2/π)/√(1+λ²). This yields the stated constant with its factor 1/(2√π); the frozen diagnostics were inspected, not used in place of the limiting proof.

value.rationale: In a model where the stationary position landscape changes with noise and tumbling, a stable single-frame decision rule is useful only with calibrated performance. This result both identifies the independent-kernel regime of stable decisions and quantitatively distinguishes the inference advantage in the athermal, crossover, and fixed thermal-noise regimes. The value lies in the observable inference transition, not in reparametrizing the previously solved stationary distribution.
